title: Extended warranty company refuses to pay for car repairs, costing customers thousands of dollars
summary: TV investigation shows a major extended auto warranty company stalling, denying, and dragging out claims while customers keep paying premiums.

assertions.quote: HE NOW KEEPS HIS VEHICLE UNDER THIS TARP AFTER IT SAT AT THE MECHANIC

verdicts.note: Lengthy third-party inspection and approval cycles for aftermarket vehicle service contracts are a widely reported complaint, echoed independently by a repair-shop owner's account of multi-week waits.

assertions.quote: WE'RE ON THE PHONE FOR 2 HOURS AND WE GET BOUNCE FROM PERSON TO PERSON.

verdicts.note: Long hold times and transfers are a common complaint pattern in vehicle-warranty disputes, though exact hours here are a single anecdote.

assertions.quote: HE REFUSES TO WORK WITH CARSHIELD AND MOST EXTENDED WARRANTY COMPANIES ANYMORE.

verdicts.note: Some shops do blacklist slow-paying administrators, but many others still accept them when reimbursement is workable, so this holds for a subset of shops rather than universally.

assertions.quote: CARSHIELD $110 A MONTH FOR AN EXTENDED WARRANTY THAT WAS SUPPOSED TO PAY FOR REPAIRS

verdicts.note: Paying for coverage that is later denied is a frequently documented outcome in vehicle service-contract complaints and FTC enforcement cases.

assertions.quote: CARSHIELD HAD THE ENGINE BROKEN DOWN NOT ONCE BUT TWICE.

verdicts.note: Repeat failures happen but aren't a distinctive consequence of using a warranty versus any repair; this is one anecdote, not a general pattern.
